objects.name: Chipkin Example B-LSC
objects.note: the device itself; the instance is configurable with --deviceID. The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with, the live object list and address-binding table. Number_Of_APDU_Retries is served by the app as 3 (12.11.29 suggested default; the stack default of 0 would never retransmit a ConfirmedEventNotification). The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation, system status and database revision; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so this example does not

objects.name: Amber
objects.note: The smoke detector. F-LIFESAFETY / F-ALARM-LS (canonical: B-LSC). Tracking_Value follows the SIMULATED detector (main.cpp section 1b: quiet(0) / alarm(2) / fault(3)); Present_Value LATCHES alarm until a LifeSafetyOperation RESET, which is refused (OBJECT / INVALID_OPERATION_IN_THIS_STATE) while the detector still sees smoke or when nothing is latched; a fault follows the detector and is not latched. Present_Value and Tracking_Value are read-only (Table 12-18). Silenced and Operation_Expected (SILENCE while sounding, RESET once silenced) follow LifeSafetyOperation. Reliability is served by the stack: this example's callback supplies the first stage (cl. 13.2.2.2, hardware - always no-fault-detected here) and the stack's FAULT_LIFE_SAFETY algorithm the second (MULTI_STATE_FAULT while Present_Value is fault). Mode is required-writable and accepted unconditionally (no customer-facing Accepted_Modes setter exists - see the file header); Accepted_Modes is therefore accepted at the stack's generic default. Event_State is NOT actually a stack default here - it is genuinely computed by the CHANGE_OF_LIFE_SAFETY and FAULT_LIFE_SAFETY algorithms this example arms; it is marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic table does not know an algorithm was armed (same convention as B-AAC's Diamond). Present_Value is also DS-COV-B subscribable

objects.name: Azure
objects.note: The smoke detector's zone. F-LIFESAFETY / F-ALARM-LS. Rolls up Life Safety Point 1 (Amber): takes its detector reading, latches alarm the same way, and a LifeSafetyOperation addressed to the zone also operates Amber. Event_State is genuinely computed (the same two algorithms are armed on Azure), marked accepted for the same generator-limitation reason. Reliability as Amber's. Zone_Members (cl. 12.16.26, required, BACnetLIST of BACnetDeviceObjectReference) should list Amber but reads as an empty list at 64b2cfac5: the stack serves it, but only the test-tool BACnetStackTestTool_SetLifeSafetyZoneMembers can fill it, and the series does not use the test-tool interface. [KNOWN GAP] in tests/life_safety_test.py; see TODO.md and stack #2036 (open)

objects.name: Crimson
objects.note: Priority, Ack_Required and Recipient_List are NOT stack DEFAULTS - they are genuinely populated, by BACnetStack_AddNotificationClassObject (Priority, Ack_Required) and BACnetStack_AddRecipientToNotificationClass (Recipient_List) at start-up. They are marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic per-type table does not know about this object-specific host-configuration API and so cannot credit them as stack-served. Routes Amber's and Azure's CHANGE_OF_LIFE_SAFETY / fault notifications, CONFIRMED, to one recipient named by DEVICE instance: 389107, the operator workstation (the stack resolves its address from its I-Am). Not writable: a B-LSC is not required to support modification of its event reporting (L.5.2)

objects.name: Vermilion
objects.note: BACnet/IP; Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal)
